shortDescription: Taiwan's Asustek Computer TWSE:2357 is launching a $1.5 billion five-year zero-coupon convertible bond, with proceeds earmarked for buying raw materials in foreign currencies, according to a term sheet seen on Thursday.Here are more details:($1 = 31.5740 Taiwan dollars)

children: is launching a $1.5 billion five-year zero-coupon convertible bond, with proceeds earmarked for buying raw materials in foreign currencies, according to a term sheet seen on Thursday.
The bonds, due in September 2031, are marketed with a yield of 0.7% to 1.7% a year and a conversion premium of 40% to 50% over Thursday's closing share price of T$989 ($31.32).
The initial conversion price is T$1,384.60 to T$1,483.50 per share.
Investors can sell the bonds back to Asustek after two years and again after four years.
